title: Remark
body_md:
The above ratio mixing property also holds for the so-called \emph{high-temperature expansion} of the Ising model (also known as loop $O(1)$ model), since it has the same distribution as the set of edges where a current sampled from $\mathbf{P}_{\beta}$ takes an odd value  (see e.g.~\cite{AizenmanDuminilTassionWarzelEmergentPlanarity2019}). 
 Mixing for this representation was recently derived in \cite{hansen2026supercritical} using different methods, but relying on the results of \cite{DGR20}.

body_md: By the domain Markov property of the respective measures, Corollary~\ref{cor: perco ratio mixing} readily implies that if $f_n^{S}$ (resp. $g_n^\xi$) denotes the Randon--Nikodym derivative between the measures $\mathbf{P}^S_{\Lambda_{2n}[\beta]}$ and $\mathbf{P}_\beta$ (resp. $\phi^\xi_{\Lambda_{2n}[\beta]}$ and $\phi_\beta$) restricted to $\Lambda_n$, then $\sup_{S\subset \partial\Lambda_{2n}} \|1-f^S_n\|_{\infty} \leq e^{-cn}$ (resp. $\sup_{\xi\in \mathrm{Part}({\partial\Lambda_{2n}})} \|1-g^\xi_n\|_{\infty} \leq e^{-cn}$). In particular, this also implies a corresponding exponential upper bound on their total variation distance.

label: prop:coupling
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:coupling}
Let $0\leq \beta'<\beta$. There exists $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(\beta,\beta')>0$ such that the following holds. For every finite subsets $S\subset \Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$, if $\mathbf{n}\sim \mathbf{P}^{S}_{\Lambda[\beta]}$ and $\mathbf{m}\sim\mathbf{P}^{S}_{ \tilde{\Lambda}[\beta,\beta']}$ then $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is distributed as the union of $\hat{\mathbf{m}}$ with an independent \textup{Ber}$(\varepsilon)$ percolation on $\Lambda$.

body_md:
\label{prop:uniform connectivity}
 	For every $\beta'>\beta_c$, there exists $c=c(\beta')>0$ such that, for every $\beta>\beta'$, every $N \geq 2n$, every $x \in \Lambda_{N-n}$, and every even $A,B\subset \partial \Lambda_{N}$, we have
 	$$\mathbf{P}^{A, B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'],

label: eq:currents equality
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\beta,\beta', \Lambda, S$ be as in the statement and recall that $\xi>0$ is chosen so that $\tanh(\xi)^2=\tanh(\beta-\beta')$. We begin by defining two maps $f$ and $g$ on $\tilde{\Lambda}[\beta,\beta']$ and $\Lambda[\beta,\beta']$ respectively.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[$\bullet$] Fix $\mathbf{m}\in \Omega_{\tilde{\Lambda}[\beta,\beta']}$. Let $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}=f(\mathbf{m})$ be the current on $\tilde{\Lambda}[\beta,\beta']$ defined as follows: for every $xy\in E(\Lambda)$, $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xy)=\mathbf{m}(xy)$; and (recall that $z=z(xy)$) $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xz)=\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(yz)=0$ if $\mathbf{m}(xz)$ and $\mathbf{m}(yz)$ are even, and $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xz)=\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(yz)=1$ if $\mathbf{m}(xz)$ and $\mathbf{m}(yz)$ are odd (note that $\mathbf{m}(xz)$ and $\mathbf{m}(yz)$ must have the same parity due to sources constraints).
    \item[$\bullet$] Fix $\mathbf{n}\in \Omega_{\Lambda[\beta,\beta']}$. Let $\tilde{\mathbf{n}}=g(\mathbf{n})$ be the current on $\Lambda[\beta,\beta']$ defined as follows: for every $xy\in E(\Lambda)$, $\tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta'))=\mathbf{n}(xy(\beta'))$, and $\tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta-\beta'))=\mathds{1}\{\mathbf{n}(xy(\beta-\beta'))\textup{ is odd}\}$. 
\end{enumerate}
Consider the normalised weights
$$
w(\tilde{\mathbf{n}})=\frac{\sum_{\mathbf{n}\in g^{-1}(\tilde{\mathbf{n}})}w(\mathbf{n})}{\cosh(\beta-\beta')^{|E(\Lambda)|}},
$$
and 
$$
w(\tilde{\mathbf{m}})=\frac{\sum_{\mathbf{m}\in f^{-1}(\tilde{\mathbf{m}})}w(\mathbf{m})}{\cosh(\xi)^{2|E(\Lambda)|}}
$$
of $\tilde{\mathbf{n}}$ and $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}$, and note that we can rewrite them in the form
$$
w(\tilde{\mathbf{n}})=\prod_{xy\in E(\Lambda)} \frac{(\beta')^{\tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta'))}}{\tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta'))!} \tanh(\beta-\beta')^{\tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta-\beta'))},
$$
and 
$$
w(\tilde{\mathbf{m}})=\prod_{xy\in E(\Lambda)} \frac{(\beta')^{\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xy(\beta'))}}{\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xy(\beta'))!} \tanh(\xi)^{\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xz(\xi))} \tanh(\xi)^{\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(yz(\xi))}.
$$
By the definition of $f$ above and due to the source constraints (the midpoints $z=z(xy)$ of $\tilde{\Lambda}[\beta,\beta']$ are not sources), we have $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xz)=\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(yz)$. Hence, our choice $\tanh(\xi)^2=\tanh(\beta-\beta')$ implies that if 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:currents equality}
\tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta'))=\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xy(\beta')) \quad \text{and} \quad \tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta-\beta'))=\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xz)(=\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(yz)) \quad \forall\, xy\in E(\Lambda),    
\end{equation}
then $w(\tilde{\mathbf{n}})=w(\tilde{\mathbf{m}})$. This in turn implies that we can find a coupling $(\tilde{\mathbf{n}},\tilde{\mathbf{m}},\mathbb{Q})$ between the measures $f(\mathbf{P}^{S}_{\Lambda[\beta,\beta']})$ and $g(\mathbf{P}^{S}_{\overline{\Lambda}[\beta,\beta']})$ such that \eqref{eq:currents equality} holds $\mathbb{Q}$-almost surely. 

We now obtain a coupling between the associated percolation configurations $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{m}}$. To this end, note that conditionally on $\tilde{\mathbf{n}}$, the collection of random variables $(\mathbbm{1}\{\mathbf{n}(xy(\beta-\beta'))>0\})_{xy\in E(\Lambda)}$ is a sequence of independent Bernoulli random variables that take the value $1$ if $\tilde{\mathbf{n}}(xy(\beta-\beta'))=1$ and are otherwise equal to $1$ with a certain probability $p_1$, which does not depend on the edge $xy$. Similarly, conditionally on $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}$, the collection of random variables $(\mathbbm{1}\{\mathbf{m}(xz(xy))\mathbf{m}(yz(xy))>0\})_{xy\in E(\Lambda)}$ is a sequence of independent Bernoulli random variables that take the value $1$ if $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}(xz(xy))=1$ and otherwise take the value $1$ with a certain probability $p_2$. It suffices to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq: p_1>p_2}
p_1>p_2.
\end{equation}
Indeed, assume \eqref{eq: p_1>p_2}. Using the coupling between $\tilde{\mathbf{n}}$ and $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}$ that satisfies \eqref{eq:currents equality}, we can couple the random variables $(\mathbbm{1}\{\mathbf{n}(xy(\beta-\beta'))>0\})_{xy\in E(\Lambda)}$ and $(\mathbbm{1}\{\mathbf{m}(xz(\xi))\mathbf{m}(yz(\xi))>0\})_{xy\in E(\Lambda)}$ so that the former is equal to the union of the latter with an independent Bernoulli percolation on $E(\Lambda)$ of parameter $\varepsilon=\frac{p_1-p_2}{1-p_2}$. The existence of the desired coupling between $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{m}}$ then follows.

Let us now prove \eqref{eq: p_1>p_2}. Using the identity $\rm{sech}^2(\xi):=\frac{1}{\cosh(\xi)^2}=1-\tanh(\xi)^2$, we get
\[
p_2=\left(1-\frac{1}{\cosh(\xi)}\right)^2=1-2\sqrt{1-\tanh(\xi)^2}+1-\tanh(\xi)^2.
\]
Let $t:=\beta-\beta'$. One has
\[
p_1=1-\frac{1}{\cosh(t)}.
\]
Since $\tanh(\xi)^2=\tanh(t)$ by our choice of $\xi$, $1-\tanh(t)=e^{-t}/\cosh(t)$, and $4e^{-t}\cosh(t)=2+2e^{-2t}$,
\[
p_1-p_2=-\frac{1}{\cosh(t)}+\sqrt{\frac{4e^{-t}}{\cosh(t)}}-\frac{e^{-t}}{\cosh(t)}=\frac{1}{\cosh(t)}\left(\sqrt{2+2e^{-2t}}-1-e^{-t}\right).
\]
Now, for $t>0$,
\[
2+2e^{-2t}-(1+e^{-t})^2=1-2e^{-t}+e^{-2t}>0,
\]
which implies that $p_1>p_2$. This completes the proof.

name: \hspace{1pt

title: Proof
body_md:
If $\Lambda_n(x)\cap\Lambda_n(y)\ne\emptyset$, then the result is straightforward, so we assume that $\Lambda_n(x)\cap\Lambda_n(y)=\emptyset$. 
                                                                                                                                                                                            
Consider the graph $\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}$ defined above.
By the switching lemma (see Lemma \ref{lem:switching}), 
\begin{equation}
	\label{eq:collapsed_dc1}
	\mathbf{P}^{S, \emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}, \Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}[{\bf x}\xleftrightarrow[]{\widehat{\mathbf{n}_1 + \mathbf{n}_2}\:} {\bf y}]=\frac{\langle{\sigma_{{\bf x}}\sigma_{{\bf y}}\sigma_S}\rangle_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}\,\langle{\sigma_{{\bf x}}\sigma_{{\bf y}}}\rangle_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}}{\langle{\sigma_S}\rangle_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}}\ge \langle{\sigma_{{\bf x}}\sigma_{{\bf y}}}\rangle_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}^2,
\end{equation}
	where in the second inequality we used Griffiths' inequalities (see Proposition~\ref{prop: Griffiths}). By the Edwards--Sokal coupling (see Section \ref{sec:preliminaries}) we have
	$$
    \langle{\sigma_{{\bf x}}\sigma_{{\bf y}}}\rangle_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}=\phi_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}[{\bf x}\longleftrightarrow{\bf y}].
    $$
    Note that we can view $\phi_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}$ as the measure $\phi_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}$ with edges in $\Lambda_{n/2}(x)\cup\Lambda_{n/2}(y)$ conditioned to be open (an event we call $\mathcal{E}_1$), and similarly we can view $\phi_{\Lambda_N[\beta']}$ as the measure $\phi_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}$ with edges not labelled as $\beta'$ conditioned to be closed (an event we call $\mathcal{E}_2$).
    Thus, applying the FKG inequality twice we obtain
    \begin{align}\label{eq:k}
    \begin{aligned}\langle{\sigma_{{\bf x}}\sigma_{{\bf y}}}\rangle_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}&=\phi_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\Lambda_{n/2}(x)\longleftrightarrow \Lambda_{n/2}(y)\: |\: \mathcal{E}_1]\\&\ge \phi_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\Lambda_{n/2}(x)\longleftrightarrow \Lambda_{n/2}(y)]
    \\&\ge \phi_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\Lambda_{n/2}(x)\longleftrightarrow \Lambda_{n/2}(y)\: |\: \mathcal{E}_2]
    \\&= \phi_{\Lambda_N[\beta']}[\Lambda_{{n/2}}(x)\longleftrightarrow\Lambda_{{n/2}}(y)]\ge 1-\exp(-cn^{d-1}),
    \end{aligned}\end{align}
    for some constant $c>0$,
	where the last inequality follows from \cite{Bod05} as explained in Remark \ref{rem: connectivity fk}.
	
	Now, let us prove that for every $n$ large enough we have that
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:kk}
    \mathbf{P}^{S, \emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'],\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\mathcal E]\le e^{c' n^{d-1}}\mathbf{P}^{S, \emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}, \Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}[\mathcal E]
    \end{equation}
    for some constant $c'<c/2$,
    where $\mathcal{E}=\{\Lambda_{n}(x)\xleftrightarrow[]{\widehat{\mathbf{n}_1 + \mathbf{n}_2}\:} \Lambda_{n}(y)\}^c$.
	This would be enough to conclude, since we can combine \eqref{eq:k} and \eqref{eq:collapsed_dc1}, and then use \eqref{eq:kk} to obtain that 
	$$\mathbf{P}^{S, \emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\mathcal{E}]\le e^{c' n^{d-1}}\mathbf{P}^{S, \emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}, \Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}[\mathcal{E}]\le e^{c'n^{d-1}}\mathbf{P}^{S,\emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet},\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}[\{\mathbf{x}\xleftrightarrow[]{\widehat{\mathbf{n}_1+\mathbf{n}_2}\:} \mathbf{y}\}^c]\leq {2} e^{-c' n^{d-1}}.$$
We therefore focus on proving \eqref{eq:kk}. Let $\Lambda \coloneqq \Lambda_n(x) \cup \Lambda_n(y)$ and let $E$ denote the set of edges in $\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']$ that do not lie in $\tilde{\Lambda}$. Consider a current ${\bf m}\in \mathbb{N}^E$ with $\partial {\bf m}\subset\partial\Lambda$ and define $\mathcal E_{\bf m}$ to be the event
that $\mathbf{n}$ is equal to ${\bf m}$ on $E$. Rewriting the weights we obtain that 
\begin{align*}
\frac{\mathbf{P}^{\emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\mathcal E_{\bf m}]}{\mathbf{P}^{\emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}[\mathcal E_{\bf m}]}&=\frac{\langle{\sigma_{\partial{\bf m}}}\rangle_{(\Lambda_{n}(x)\cup\Lambda_{n}(y))[\beta]}}{\langle{\sigma_{\partial{\bf m}}}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(x)\cup\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(y)}}\,\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{m}' \in  \mathbb{N}^E: \, \partial\mathbf{m}'\subset\partial\Lambda}w_\beta(\mathbf{m}')\langle{\sigma_{\partial\mathbf{m}'}}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(x)\cup\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(y)}}{\displaystyle\sum_{\mathbf{m}' \in  \mathbb{N}^E: \, \partial\mathbf{m}'\subset\partial\Lambda}w_\beta(\mathbf{m}')\langle{\sigma_{\partial\mathbf{m}'}}\rangle_{(\Lambda_{n}(x)\cup\Lambda_{n}(y))[\beta]}}\\
&\le \max_{\substack{A\subset\partial\Lambda_{n}(x)\\ |A|\text{ even}}}\frac{\langle{\sigma_A}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(x)}}{\langle{\sigma_A}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}(x)[\beta]}}\times\max_{\substack{B\subset\partial\Lambda_{n}(y)\\ |B|\text{ even}}}\frac{\langle{\sigma_B}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(y)}}{\langle{\sigma_B}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}(y)[\beta]}},
\end{align*}
where we used Griffiths' inequality (see Proposition~\ref{prop: Griffiths}) to argue that $\langle{\sigma_{\partial{\bf m}}}\rangle_{(\Lambda_{n}(x)\cup\Lambda_{n}(y))[\beta]}\leq \langle{\sigma_{\partial{\bf m}}}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(x)\cup\Lambda_{n}^\bullet(y)}$.
A similar bound can be derived for $\mathbf{P}^{S}_{\Lambda_N[\beta,\beta']}$ and $\mathbf{P}^{S}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}$ instead of $\mathbf{P}^{\emptyset}_{\Lambda_N[\beta,\beta']}$ and $\mathbf{P}^{\emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}$. We deduce, by decomposing on possible values of $(\mathbf{n}_1,\mathbf{n}_2)$ on $E$ that satisfy the event $\mathcal{E}$, 
$$\mathbf{P}^{S, \emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\mathcal E]\le  \Bigg(\max_{\substack{A\subset\partial\Lambda_{n}\\ |A|\text{ even}}}\frac{\langle{\sigma_A}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}^\bullet}}{\langle{\sigma_A}\rangle_{\Lambda_{n}[\beta]}}\Bigg)^4\ \mathbf{P}^{S, \emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}, \Lambda_N^{\bullet\bullet}}[\mathcal E],$$
so that \eqref{eq:kk} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:weak weak mix}.

label: eq:current monotonicity
title: Proof
body_md:
The result holds trivially if $\Lambda_n(x)\cap \partial \Lambda_{N-2n}\neq \emptyset$, so let us assume that $\Lambda_n(x)\cap \partial \Lambda_{N-2n}= \emptyset$.
It follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:connectivity_old} that     
$$\mathbf{P}^{A, \emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\Lambda_n(x)\xleftrightarrow[]{\widehat{\mathbf{n}_1 + \mathbf{n}_2}\:} \partial \Lambda_{N-2n}] \geq 1 - e^{-cn^{d-1}}\,.$$
To conclude, it therefore suffices to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:current monotonicity}
\mathbf{P}^{A, B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\Lambda_n(x)\xleftrightarrow[]{\widehat{\mathbf{n}_1 + \mathbf{n}_2}\:} \partial \Lambda_{N-2n}] \geq \mathbf{P}^{A, \emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\Lambda_n(x)\xleftrightarrow[]{\widehat{\mathbf{n}_1 + \mathbf{n}_2}\:} \partial \Lambda_{N-2n}].
\end{equation}
A similar statement appeared in \cite[Lemma~3.3]{duminil2021conformal}. Let $\mathsf{C}$ denote the union of all clusters that intersect $\Lambda_n(x)$. Consider a set of vertices $C$ (of $\widetilde{\Lambda}_N[\beta,\beta']$) that contains $\Lambda_n(x)$ and does not intersect the annulus $\Lambda_N\setminus\Lambda_{N-2n-1}$ (i.e. a potential realisation of $\mathsf{C}$ under the event $\{\Lambda_n(x)\xleftrightarrow[]{\widehat{\mathbf{n}_1 + \mathbf{n}_2}\:} \partial \Lambda_{N-2n}\}^c$). Write $\mathbf{C}$ for the set of vertices that lie either in $C$ or are adjacent to an element of $C$. Note that we may view $\mathbf{C}$ as a sub-weighted graph of $\widetilde{\Lambda}_N[\beta,\beta']$. Then, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prob cluster}
\mathbf{P}^{A, B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\mathsf{C}=C]=\frac{Z^{\emptyset,\emptyset}_{\mathbf{C},\mathbf{C}}[\mathsf{C}=C]Z^{A}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}Z^{B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}}{Z^{A}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}Z^{B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}}.
\end{equation}
Recall that 
\[Z^{B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}=2^{-|\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']|}Z^{\textup{Ising}}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\sigma_B] \]
and
\[Z^{B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}=2^{-|\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']|+|\mathbf{C}|}Z^{\textup{Ising}}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}[\sigma_B] .
\] 
We can express $Z^{\textup{Ising}}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\sigma_B]$ as $Z^{\textup{Ising}}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}[\sigma_B G(\sigma)]$, where 
\[
G(\sigma)=\sum_{\tau\in \{\pm 1\}^{\mathbf{C}}}\prod_{xy\in E(\mathbf{C})} e^{J_{xy} \tau_x\tau_y}\prod_{xy\in \partial_E \mathbf{C}} e^{J_{xy}\tau_x\sigma_y},
\]
where $J$ is defined as above Figure \ref{fig:doubleedge} and $\partial_E \mathbf{C}$ denotes the edges of $\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']$ with one endpoint in $\mathbf{C}$ and one endpoint outside. By Taylor expanding $e^{J_{xy}\tau_x\sigma_y}$ and using Griffiths' inequality (see Proposition~\ref{prop: Griffiths}), we obtain that $\langle \sigma_B G(\sigma)\rangle_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus\mathbf{C}}\geq \langle \sigma_B \rangle_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}\langle G(\sigma)\rangle_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}$. 
Thus,
\begin{align*}
\frac{Z^{B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}}{Z^{B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}}&=2^{|\mathbf{C}|}\frac{\langle \sigma_B G(\sigma)\rangle_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}}{\langle \sigma_B\rangle_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}}\\&\geq 2^{|\mathbf{C}|} \langle G(\sigma)\rangle_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}=\frac{Z^{\emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}}{Z^{\emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']\setminus \mathbf{C}}}.
\end{align*}
Combining the above inequality with \eqref{eq:prob cluster} we deduce that
\[
\mathbf{P}^{A, B}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\mathsf{C}=C]\leq \mathbf{P}^{A, \emptyset}_{\widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta'], \widetilde{\Lambda_N}[\beta,\beta']}[\mathsf{C}=C].
\]
Summing over all $C$ that contain $\Lambda_n(x)$ and do not intersect the annulus $\Lambda_N\setminus\Lambda_{N-2n-1}$, and then taking complements, we obtain \eqref{eq:current monotonicity}, which completes the proof.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\beta>\beta_c$ and $n\geq 1$.
Recall the coarse-grained percolation model $\eta^L$ constructed below Theorem~\ref{thm:unique_currents} and import all the notations from there. We fix $L$ large enough so that $\eta^L$ stochastically dominates a Bernoulli site percolation with parameter $p$, which in turn is chosen close enough to $1$ (namely $p>1-p_c^{\textup{site}}(\mathbb Z^d)$) so that the existence of closed paths decays exponentially fast in the distance.

$\bullet$ \textbf{Step 1.} We start by proving \eqref{eq:truncated} for $A$ of even cardinality. 
Let $N>2n$ to be taken large enough. By Corollary~\ref{coro:expression truncated switching} we have
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:truncated proof}
     \langle\sigma_A;\sigma_B\rangle_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}^+
     = \langle\sigma_A\sigma_B\rangle_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}^+ \mathbf{P}^{A\cup B, \emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta],\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]}[\mathcal{F}_A^{\mathrm{c}}].
 \end{equation}
Due to the sources constraint and the parity of $|A|$, the event $\mathcal{F}_A^{\mathrm{c}}$ implies the existence of two disjoint clusters connecting $A$ and $B$, thus in particular crossing the annulus $\Lambda_{2n}\setminus\Lambda_n$. However, this cannot happen if there exists a blocking surface (i.e.~a cutset) $\eta^L$-open sites separating the inner and outer boundaries of the annulus. By the aforementioned comparison with Bernoulli percolation, the latter event holds with probability at least $1-e^{-cn}$, thus concluding the proof of \eqref{eq:truncated}.

$\bullet$ \textbf{Step 2.} We now turn to \eqref{eq:truncated_pt_to_pt}. Fix $N>|x|$, so that $x\in\Lambda_N$. We have
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:truncated_proof}
     \langle\sigma_0;\sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} = \frac{Z^{\{0,x\}}_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]} Z^\emptyset_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]} - Z^{\{0,\mathfrak{g}\}}_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]} Z^{\{x,\mathfrak{g}\}}_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]}}{(Z^\emptyset_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]})^2} = \langle\sigma_0\sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} \mathbf{P}^{\{0,x\}, \emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta],\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]}[0\mathrel{\mathop{\centernot\longleftrightarrow}_{}^{}} \mathfrak{g}],
 \end{equation}
where the last equality follows readily from Lemma~\ref{lem:switching}. 
Due to the comparison with a highly supercritical Bernoulli percolation, with probability at least $1-e^{-c|x|}$, there exists an $\eta^L$-open blocking surface separating\footnote{Recall the definition, for a set $S\subset \mathbb Z^d$, of $S_L=\{z\in\Lambda_{\tilde{N}}:~\Lambda_{10 L}(Lz)\cap S\neq\emptyset\}$, introduced below Theorem~\ref{thm:unique_currents}.}  $\{0\}_L$ and $\{x\}_L$,
which in turn is also connected to $\partial \Lambda_{\tilde{N}}$ (where we recall that $\tilde{N}=\lfloor N/L\rfloor-10$) in at least $c \tilde{N}^{d-1}\gg |x|$ many points for some $c>0$. Conditionally on this event, a simple insertion tolerance argument gives that the $\eta$-cluster induced by this $\eta^L$-cluster is connected to $\mathfrak{g}$ with probability at least $1-e^{-c|x|}$. However, on this event, any path from $0$ to $x$ in $\eta$ (which exists due to the source constraint) must be connected to $\mathfrak{g}$. This yields that $\mathbf{P}^{\{0,x\}, \emptyset}_{\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta],\Lambda_N^\mathfrak{g}[\beta]}[0\mathrel{\mathop{\centernot\longleftrightarrow}_{}^{}} \mathfrak{g}] \leq e^{-c|x|}$, concluding the proof of \eqref{eq:truncated_pt_to_pt}.

$\bullet$ \textbf{Step 3.} Finally, we use Steps 1 and 2 to prove the exponential ratio mixing for $A$ of odd cardinality. Fix $c=c(\beta,d)>0$ which satisfies the conclusions of Steps 1 and 2. Let $A\subset \Lambda_n$ of odd cardinality, $x\in A$, and $B\subset \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus \Lambda_{2n}$. By the Lebowitz inequality (see Proposition \ref{prop: lebowitz} and Remark \ref{rem:twist of lebowitz}),
\[
\langle \sigma_A \sigma_B |\: \sigma_x=1\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} - \langle \sigma_A \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\geq \Big|\langle \sigma_A |\: \sigma_x=1\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}-\langle \sigma_B |\: \sigma_x=1\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_A \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\Big|.
\]
Writing $\mathbbm{1}_{\sigma_x=1}=\frac{\sigma_x+1}{2}$ and multiplying both sides of the above equation by $2\langle \mathds{1}_{\sigma_x=1}\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}$ yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq: Lebowitz}
\langle \sigma_A \sigma_B \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} - \langle \sigma_A \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\geq \Big|\langle \sigma_A  \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}-\langle \sigma_B \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_A \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\Big|.
\end{equation}
Rearranging and using that $\sigma_x^2=1$ (so that $\sigma_A\sigma_x=\sigma_{A\setminus \{x\}}$ since $x\in A$) we obtain
\[
\langle \sigma_A \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\leq \langle \sigma_{A\setminus \{x\}}\sigma_B\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}-\langle \sigma_{A\setminus\{x\}}\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}+\langle \sigma_B \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_A \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}.
\]
Now, since $A\setminus \{x\}$ is even, by Step 1, 
\[
\langle \sigma_{A\setminus \{x\}}\sigma_B\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}-\langle \sigma_{A\setminus\{x\}}\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\leq e^{-cn}\langle \sigma_{A\setminus\{x\}}\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\leq e^{-cn}\frac{\langle \sigma_A\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}}{\langle \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}},
\]
where we used Griffiths' inequality (see Proposition \ref{prop: Griffiths}) in the last inequality. It remains to prove that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq: target}
\langle \sigma_B \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\leq (1+e^{-cn})\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]},
\end{equation}
from which the desired result follows (with potentially a different constant $c$). To this end, take $y\in \Lambda_n$ such that $\lVert y-x \rVert \geq n$ and apply \eqref{eq: Lebowitz} for $A=\{y\}$. By rearranging, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:last equ proof trunc}
\langle \sigma_B \sigma_x\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_y  \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} \leq \langle \sigma_x \sigma_y \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} - \langle \sigma_y \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}+\langle \sigma_x  \sigma_y\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}.
\end{equation}
By  Griffiths' inequality, the exponential ratio mixing we proved above for $A$ of even cardinality in Step 1, and the exponential decay of truncated $2$-point functions from Step 2, 
\begin{align*}
\langle \sigma_x \sigma_y \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} &- \langle \sigma_y \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}
\\&\leq 
\langle \sigma_x \sigma_y \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]} - \langle \sigma_y  \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}
\\ 
&\leq \Big(\langle \sigma_x\sigma_y\rangle_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}^+-\langle \sigma_y  \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\Big)\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}+e^{-cn}\langle \sigma_x\sigma_y\rangle_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}^+\langle \sigma_B\rangle_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}^+
\\
&\leq 3e^{-cn}\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle  \sigma_y \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}.
\end{align*}
Using again Step 2, we obtain 
\[
\langle \sigma_x  \sigma_y\rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\leq (1+e^{-cn})\langle \sigma_x \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle  \sigma_y \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}\langle \sigma_B \rangle^+_{\Lambda_N[\beta]}.
\]
Combining the two previous equations and \eqref{eq:last equ proof trunc} yields \eqref{eq: target}, thus completing the proof.
